subtitle: For the record: every branch susceptance of a 70,000-bus synthetic grid, recovered from one port as the exact rational number in its source file, from 224,332 readings instead of 2.45 billion
absresult: Ten public grids from 118 to 70,000 buses, 172,819 unknowns in all, are identified and recovered exactly over $\mathbb Q$ with zero mismatches against the MATPOWER source. The largest is ACTIVSg 70k: 83,318 unknowns from 224,332 readings, which is 10,921 times fewer than the $n(n+1)/2=2{,}449{,}965{,}000$ of the unknown-network protocol and 2.69 readings per unknown. Its filled factor has 33.4 million entries per prime, and the whole run takes under 50 minutes on two cores. Along the way the data forced two structural results. Islands joined to the grid only through the reference bus are invisible from any port. Harmonic pockets, $K_4$ blocks whose two interior buses have no ground and no outside branch, each cost one rank until a source is placed inside them (Lemma XIII.2.2). The kernel locates both, and the loop places the sources.
rectext: Every grid in the table is identified and recovered exactly. The number of readings per unknown stays between 2.46 and 3.24 from 118 buses to 70,000, so the readings grow linearly with the grid, while the unknown-network protocol grows quadratically. The saving factor therefore rises with size: 16 on IEEE 118, 975 on PEGASE 9241, and 10,921 on ACTIVSg 70k. The extra sources vary by structure. The two ACTIVSg grids at 25k and 70k need only 92 and 125, while the PEGASE grids at 9241 and 13659 need 1,257 each. In every case the number is whatever the kernel loop asks for, and on the PEGASE grids that includes the interiors of the harmonic pockets. The precision needed varies by source format as well. The ACTIVSg reactances have heights of at most 26 bits and stop at 3 primes. The PEGASE and RTE values reach 63–64 bits and stop at 6 primes, which the early-terminating rule finds with no knowledge of the answer.
suretext:
Status XIII.5.1 (what is now certain, grid by grid) verified · exact

On all ten grids the recovered rationals equal the MATPOWER source exactly. Two complete runs agree hash for hash, with different fill-reducing orderings, different elimination trees and disjoint families of primes. On every grid up to buses, full rank has also been re-derived by verifiers that share no code with the kernel: two of them up to 6,515 buses, one beyond. The negative index of $K$ is certified exactly for every indefinite grid up to 25,000 buses, and on ACTIVSg 70k under an explicit a priori rounding bound. Proposition XIII.1.1 removes the passivity hypothesis from the physical protocol on every grid. Above buses, which leaves ACTIVSg 25k and 70k, identifiability rests on the kernel alone. It is cross-checked by the second ordering, the second prime family, the overdetermined consistency of every generated row, and exact agreement with the source. A dense verifier for those two grids would need 5 and 39 GB for $G$ alone, which this machine does not have.
sureabs: Every result above survives four further checks. Two verifiers that share no code with the kernel re-derive full rank, up to 6,515 buses with both and beyond that with one. A second fill-reducing ordering and a disjoint family of primes recover the identical rationals on all ten grids, hash for hash. The negative index of $K$ is certified exactly, and it equals the number of negative merged branches. A new root-selection proposition (XIII.1.1) makes the Part VIII protocol valid on the indefinite grids at weak enough interventions. The harmonic-pocket proposition (XIII.2.2) is confirmed exactly on planted pockets in random host networks and as a necessary condition on all ten grids.
